title: The stUSDS Distribution Reward makes borrowers fund the referral fee paid to Prime Agents
content:
A.4.4.1.3.7 defines the stUSDS Distribution Reward as an incentive "designed to encourage Prime Agents and Integrators to promote stUSDS adoption," calculated as a percentage of the stUSDS balance associated with a Reward Code, "initially set at 0.1% in total." It is paid to the Prime Agent, with any share for the Integrator left to bilateral negotiation.

The structurally interesting part is where the cost lands. The same quantity appears as a term in the SKY Borrow Minimum Rate (A.4.4.1.3.5.2), which means the floor on borrowing costs rises by exactly the referral rate. Borrowers pay for the growth of the lender base.

That routing is deliberate and defensible. A referral paid out of lender yield would reduce the advertised stUSDS Rate and partially defeat the purpose of the incentive — you would be funding acquisition by making the product worse. Embedding it in the borrower's floor keeps the supply-side proposition intact and treats distribution as a cost of running the facility, recovered like any other.

It also composes cleanly with the no-arbitrage argument: the floor must cover the *total* cost of capital, and an obligation to pay 0.1% to whoever sourced the deposit is part of that cost. Leaving it out would reopen exactly the value-draining loop the floor exists to close.

The pattern generalizes: Sky funds growth incentives by widening the spread paid by the leveraged side, and keeps the referral relationship (Prime Agent to Integrator) outside the protocol as a private negotiation rather than an on-chain split.
description: A 0.1% referral on stUSDS balances is a term inside the SKY Borrow Minimum Rate, so distribution costs are recovered from borrowers rather than netted out of lender yield.
